conventions: A postposed אֶחָד/אַחַת that the ASV renders by nothing but the indefinite article ('a cake of bread', 'a portion', 'a cake of raisins') takes that 'a' itself, since a present numeral is what the word renders (rule 11); the noun keeps only its own word. The competing reading (article to the noun under rule 15, numeral unrepresented) was rejected because it leaves a lexical numeral unrendered while its English stands on the page.

Hiphil בוא → 'brought in' keeps 'in' with the verb as the lexeme-completing particle of the bring-in sense (rule 44); the surplus-particle reading marking 'in' added was considered and named in the note. Likewise 'gathered together' (6.1), 'broken forth' (6.8, with the cognate פֶּרֶץ unrepresented), 'carried aside' (6.10) and 'looked out' (6.16) keep their particles.

גֹּרֶן → 'the threshing floor' heads on 'floor' as the class noun the ASV also writes alone for the word, 'threshing' read as the specifier (rule 31 tie); 'threshing' was the available competing head. Distributive אִישׁ → 'every one' (6.19 ×2) heads on 'one' on the same reasoning.

In the ark-naming relative clause, the resumptive עָלָיו is construed with נִקְרָא per the ASV margin ('whereupon is called the Name') and dissolved into 'which'; עַל and its suffix are unrepresented (rule 22), and 'above' goes to the bare accusative הַכְּרֻבִים after יֹשֵׁב under rule 33, not to עַל.
report: Checked every candidate group in the table and the eight added units end to end; no construction is analysed two ways without a source-licensed difference.

The waw buckets are ASV connective choices (And/and/So/Then/but/with/therefore) plus four apodosis waws (6.6, 6.13, 6.18 unrepresented; 6.16 → that). All four follow rule 45's positional reading: 6.13 writes 'that' inside the frame before 'when' so the frame keeps it and the waw is bare, while 6.16 writes 'that' at the apodosis head so the waw takes it. Consistent.

Article buckets: 6.7 הַשַּׁל → 'his' (rule 41), 6.8/6.9 demonstrative phrases and 6.12/6.16 'king David' unrepresented, arthrous recta take their own 'the' (6.17, 6.20). Consistent with rule 29/41 counting.
Appositional 'even' with no marker on the appositive is added in both 6.2 (even the name) and 6.19 (even among), and the second לְ in 6.19 keeps its own 'among'. Consistent under rule 16.

לְ before infinitive: 6.2/6.20/6.21 take the written 'to'; 6.10 'would not remove' writes none and is unrepresented (rule 52). Bare accusatives בֵּית/עִיר take the supplied into/in + the in 6.10, 6.11, 6.12, 6.16 (rule 33). Consistent.

BSB disagreements are all convention: dative/possessive/temporal prepositions the ASV recasts (rule 40), unrendered articles beside demonstratives or in 'king David', object markers, apodosis waws, the resumptive suffixes of 6.2 (עָלָיו) and 6.23 (לָהּ). 6.8 פֶּרֶץ (cognate accusative) is unrepresented with 'forth' kept on פָּרַץ as the lexeme-completing particle; the alternative reading ('forth' to the cognate noun) is defensible but not an error. None is a genuine error.

Judgment calls carried across verses and worth a log entry: אֶחָד → 'a' (6.19 ×3) with the numeral taking the indefinite article rather than the noun; בוא hiphil → 'brought in' whole (6.17); גֹּרֶן → 'threshing floor' headed on 'floor'; distributive אִישׁ → 'every one' headed on 'one'. Each verse note names its competing reading.
No promotion: nothing this chapter taught generalises beyond what rules 14, 16, 33, 41, 45 and 55 already say, and the corpus tables shown confirm the chapter's treatments.
